column1: What is meant by 'online distribution' in the context of media?
column2: Any media that is sent to users using the Internet, such as via the World Wide Web or video streaming services.

column1: Netflix is an example of an online distribution service that primarily streams what type of media files?
column2: Video files containing films or television programmes.

column1: Which online audio streaming service is primarily used to distribute music and podcasts?
column2: Spotify.

column1: Besides text and images, what other media types are commonly shared on the social media platform Facebook?
column2: Photos and videos.

column1: Give an example of a mobile device platform, including the hardware and its operating system.
column2: An iPhone 13 with iOS, or a Samsung Galaxy with Android.

column1: What is a key design consideration when distributing media for mobile devices compared to desktops?
column2: The smaller screen size of mobile devices.

column1: Tablets, such as an iPad using iPadOS, are a type of _____ platform.
column2: mobile

column1: What capability distinguishes interactive televisions from older analogue televisions?
column2: They allow users to interact with them to a greater degree, including using apps and streaming services.

column1: Besides broadcast digital television, what other types of media can be distributed through interactive TVs?
column2: Video streaming services, apps, user photos, and music.

column1: What are the typical features of a media distribution kiosk?
column2: A kiosk contains a touch screen and will have limited functionality.

column1: What types of media are typically distributed through kiosks?
column2: Images, animation, and sounds.

column1: Self-service checkouts in supermarkets are a type of kiosk that primarily uses what media to identify products?
column2: They scan bar codes (images) on products.

column1: What kind of media would an information kiosk, such as one displaying a map, primarily use?
column2: Images (maps and photos), and sometimes sounds or background music.

column1: What is the primary function of an Internet kiosk often found in hotels or airports?
column2: To allow public access to websites.

column1: An advertisement display kiosk is used to show images, photos, or _____ to promote products.
column2: video

column1: What term describes media products distributed using tangible formats like DVDs or advertising posters?
column2: Physical media.

column1: Name two distinct categories of physical media mentioned in the source material.
column2: Print products (like posters) and digital media (like DVDs and Blu-Rays).

column1: List three examples of print media, other than posters.
column2: Books, magazines, flyers, newspapers, or maps.

column1: What type of media were Compact Discs (CDs) commonly used to distribute?
column2: Music.

column1: What is the approximate storage capacity of a standard Compact Disc (CD) in terms of uncompressed audio?
column2: 74 minutes or 650 MB.

column1: What are Digital Versatile Discs (DVDs) primarily used to store and distribute?
column2: Films and television programmes.

column1: A standard DVD can store up to 9.4 GB on each side, which is enough for approximately how many hours of video?
column2: Around 4 hours, depending on compression.

column1: What is another common name for a 'memory stick'?
column2: A pen drive or USB removable storage.

column1: What type of removable flash memory card is typically used in high-end digital cameras?
column2: SD cards.

column1: Which types of removable flash memory cards are most commonly used in smartphones?
column2: Mini and micro-SD cards.

column1: Under what circumstance does storage like flash memory become especially important for sharing media?
column2: When the Internet is not available.

column1: What are the four ink colours represented by the acronym CMYK, used in more expensive colour printing?
column2: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, and Key/Black.

column1: Why is distributing paper-based media significantly more expensive than distributing online media?
column2: Because it needs to be printed and physically transported.

column1: What are three potential distribution methods for a television programme, such as a natural history show?
column2: Broadcast television, Blu-Ray/DVD, and streaming platforms.

column1: Name two different distribution methods for a digital image used to advertise a programme.
column2: Digital images on websites, billboard posters, bus station posters, or in newspapers.
